summary: A 10-foot pole tower with a 10-by-10 cab was built in 1933 and removed in 1965. The sources disagree on the cab design; none describes the site today.

facts.design: 10-by-10 Aladdin L-5 cabin on a 10-foot round fir timber tower (Oregon page); register and firelookout.com say 10-foot pole L-4 tower
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1965; no source describes what remains at the site.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

events.note: 10-foot pole tower with a 10-by-10 cab; a 1933 Roseburg Chieftain item said the CCC would build it before snow
Register says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered March 19, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built 1933 at the northwest edge of the summit ridge; 10-foot pole L-4 tower; removed 1965
evidence.quote: Built in 1933 at the northwest edge of the long summit ridge, this 10' pole L-4 tower was removed in 1965.

evidence.supports: 1933 Roseburg Chieftain item: CCC to build a 10 x 10 lookout before snow
evidence.quote: A 10 x 10 lookout to be built by the CCC before the snow flies.

evidence.supports: 10 x 10 Aladdin L-5 cabin on a 10-foot round fir timber tower, 1933
evidence.quote: 1933: A 10 x 10 Aladdin L-5 lookout cabin erected atop a 10-foot round fir timber tower.
The lookout anchored by one quarter inch cables.

evidence.supports: page says only that the lookout was removed
list marks Johnson Butte (Douglas) as Tower Gone
evidence.quote: Johnson Butte Douglas 43.43305 -122.63432 Tower Gone FFLOS US 867, OR 234

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Oregon page describes a 10-by-10 Aladdin L-5 cabin on a 10-foot round fir timber tower. The register and firelookout.com describe a 10-foot pole L-4 tower. The brief's L-5 is kept because the Oregon page names it; the story reports both. The editor should decide.
The register says removed in 1965 and firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965. The Oregon page says removed with no year. The year 1965 is used.

notes_for_editor: The 1933 build and 1965 removal agree across the register and firelookout.com. The L-5 cab, the CCC plan and the cable anchoring come only from the Oregon page, which is a compiled set of clippings and quotes. Searches found no record of this lookout beyond the register and the Oregon page, and the search results were about other Douglas County lookouts. No source describes the site today. The brief's 3.0 m height matches the 10-foot tower.
